questions.question: Why are viruses called obligate intracellular agents?
options: They replicate only inside living cells
They replicate only outside living cells
They reproduce in ordinary culture media
They require both DNA and RNA

options: No clear explanation for viral origin has been confirmed

It can act directly as mRNA

options: Enter the nucleus and become DNA
Bind directly to ribosomes without modification
Serve as a template for mRNA synthesis

What is the capsid?
options: An impermeable protein shell around viral nucleic acid

questions.question: What are capsomers?
options: Protein subunits composed of polypeptide molecules

questions.question: Which is NOT a listed function of the viral capsid?
What does viral symmetry describe?
options: Capsid morphology based on capsomer arrangement

questions.question: Why is glycerol added to a viral suspension?
options: To preserve the virus during storage

questions.question: What is viral tropism?
options: Specific infection of a cell, tissue or host that supports viral replication

questions.question: Which two factors are important determinants of viral tropism?
options: Specific receptors and required transcription factors

options: Ribosomes, ATP, amino acids and nucleotides
